components.note: 夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 他讲的笑话把大家逗笑了。
example.pinyin: Tā jiǎng de xiàohua bǎ dàjiā dòuxiào le.
example.english: The joke he told made everyone laugh.
example.fact: 笑话 works as both a noun ("a joke") and a verb ("to mock, laugh at") without any change in form — 讲笑话 means "to tell a joke," while 别笑话我 means "don't make fun of me," the same two characters serving opposite grammatical roles.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
忄 (heart) — 惜 describes an emotional response felt in the heart.
昔 (the past, former times) — feeling 忄 for the past 昔 gave 惜 its meaning 'to cherish, to regret.'

example.hanzi: 可惜我们没赶上那场演出。
example.pinyin: Kěxī wǒmen méi gǎnshàng nà chǎng yǎnchū.
example.english: It's a pity we didn't catch that show.
example.fact: 可惜 usually opens a sentence as a stand-alone comment on a regrettable fact, much like English "unfortunately" — but it can also sit inside a sentence as a predicate ("这可惜了", "what a shame"), giving it more flexibility than a fixed sentence adverb.

components.note: 口 (a rock) — the boulder itself.
厂 (a cliff) — the rock lying at the base of a cliff, the source of 石's meaning 'stone, rock.'
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 小心,路上有石头。
example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, lùshang yǒu shítou.
example.english: Careful, there is a stone on the road.
example.fact: 头 as a noun suffix turns a plain root into an everyday, concrete word — 石头 ("stone"), 木头 ("wood"), 骨头 ("bone") — a pattern that leans toward materials and substances, in contrast to the suffix 子 (as in 孩子), which leans toward living or countable things.

meanings: foot (unit of length equal to 0.3048 m)

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) gives a sound hint — 英 is pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
尺 is traditionally read as a picture of a bent leg taking a measured step, used before rulers existed to pace off a distance — the origin of its meaning 'a Chinese foot, a ruler.'

example.hanzi: 这个房间大约有十英尺长。
example.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān dàyuē yǒu shí yīngchǐ cháng.
example.english: This room is about ten feet long.
example.fact: 英尺 literally reads "English chi" — 英 marks "English/British" the same way it does in 英里 ("mile") and 英镑 ("pound sterling"), repurposing 尺 (a traditional Chinese unit close to a third of a meter) to gloss a foreign measurement instead of coining an entirely new word.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 细 relates to something as fine and thin as silk thread
田 (tián) gives a loose sound connection to 细's reading xì
节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'

example.hanzi: 他向我们说明了计划的细节。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒmen shuōmíng le jìhuà de xìjié.
example.english: He explained the details of the plan to us.
example.fact: 细 ("fine, thin") plus 节 ("a joint or segment," as in a bamboo stalk or 春节) combine almost literally into "a fine segment" — one small individual unit that makes up a larger whole, which is how 细节 came to mean "detail."

components.note: 禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.

example.hanzi: 科学的发展改变了我们的生活。
example.pinyin: Kēxué de fāzhǎn gǎibiàn le wǒmen de shēnghuó.
example.english: The development of science has changed our lives.
example.fact: 科学 is one of many modern Chinese abstract terms borrowed back from Japanese: 19th-century Japanese scholars coined 科学 (kagaku, "branch of study") from the same characters to translate Western "science," and it was then re-imported into Chinese — the same path taken by 社会 ("society") and 经济 ("economy").

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.

example.hanzi: 有的人喜欢咖啡,有的人喜欢茶。
example.pinyin: Yǒude rén xǐhuan kāfēi, yǒude rén xǐhuan chá.
example.english: Some people like coffee, some like tea.
example.fact: 有的 is a bound word that needs a noun to attach to (有的人 "some people") or a doubled frame (有的...,有的...) to split a group into subsets — unlike English "some," it rarely opens a clause on its own without a following noun.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 你说的话很有道理。
example.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de huà hěn yǒu dàoli.
example.english: What you said makes a lot of sense.
example.fact: 道 ("the Way, a path") plus 理 ("the grain or pattern in jade, principle") combine into "the underlying pattern of the Way" — a compound with deep Daoist and philosophical roots that has flattened, in everyday speech, into the much more mundane "reason, common sense" of 有道理.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 船 is a vessel that travels on water, directly tied to its meaning 'ship, boat'
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 船长下令所有船员到甲板上集合。
example.pinyin: Chuánzhǎng xiàlìng suǒyǒu chuányuán dào jiǎbǎn shàng jíhé.
example.english: The captain ordered all crew members to assemble on deck.
example.fact: 长 is read zhǎng ("head, chief") here, not cháng ("long") — one of Mandarin's clearest multiple-reading traps, since the same character splits into two unrelated pronunciations depending on meaning, and shows up again in 校长 (xiàozhǎng, "principal") and 队长 (duìzhǎng, "team leader").

components.note: 欠 (breath, an open mouth exhaling) — 歌 relates to the breath used in singing.
哥 (gē) gives the sound — an exact match with 歌's reading gē.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 她从小就想当一名歌手。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xiǎng dāng yì míng gēshǒu.
example.english: She has wanted to be a singer since she was little.
example.fact: 手 as a suffix meaning "a skilled person who does X" recurs across profession words — 选手 ("athlete"), 水手 ("sailor"), 助手 ("assistant") — extending the literal "hand" into "a hand at doing something," similar to the English idiom "a good hand at X."

meanings: high ranking officer in Chinese army

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào

example.hanzi: 他被授予上校军衔。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi shòuyǔ shàngxiào jūnxián.
example.english: He was awarded the rank of colonel.
example.fact: Chinese military officer ranks are built from three base grades — 尉 (company-grade), 校 (field-grade) and 将 (general) — each split into 上/中/少 ("upper/middle/junior"), so 上校 "colonel" is structurally the upper tier of the 校 grade, parallel to 上尉 and 上将, rather than an unrelated standalone word.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 祝你今天运气好。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ jīntiān yùnqi hǎo.
example.english: Wishing you good luck today.
example.fact: When both syllables keep a full tone, yùnqì, the same two characters can instead mean "to circulate one's qi/breath" in qigong or martial-arts contexts — the everyday "luck" sense is distinguished by a neutral tone on the second syllable, yùnqi.

components.note: 丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'

example.hanzi: 这次会议的主要目的是讨论预算。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì de zhǔyào mùdì shì tǎolùn yùsuàn.
example.english: The main purpose of this meeting is to discuss the budget.
example.fact: 主 is traditionally read as a lamp's flame (丶) sitting atop its stand (王) — the person who tends that flame became "master, lord," and 主要 pairs it with 要 ("essential") to mean, roughly, "the master point" — today's ordinary word for "main, primary."

components.note: 凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'

example.hanzi: 我和同事一起吃午饭。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hé tóngshì yìqǐ chī wǔfàn.
example.english: I have lunch with my colleagues.
example.fact: 同事 literally means "share the same affairs" (同 "same" + 事 "matter") — one of a family of "same-X" relationship words built the same way, alongside 同学 ("classmate," same study) and 同乡 ("someone from the same hometown").

components.note: 食 (food) — 餐 relates directly to eating and meals.
广 (a building/shelter) — 厅 names a large room inside a building, a hall.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound close to tīng.

example.hanzi: 我们订了一家餐厅庆祝生日。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dìng le yì jiā cāntīng qìngzhù shēngrì.
example.english: We booked a restaurant to celebrate the birthday.
example.fact: 餐厅 covers both a stand-alone commercial "restaurant" and an institutional "dining hall" inside a school, office, or hotel — for a small, casual eatery Chinese instead reaches for 饭馆 or 小吃店, so 餐厅 leans toward a larger or more formal dining space.

components.note: 羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

example.hanzi: 大家都夸她是个美女。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu kuā tā shì gè měinǚ.
example.english: Everyone said she's a beautiful woman.
example.fact: 美女 has drifted from its literal "beautiful woman" into a casual, almost gender-neutral form of address across much of Mainland China — shop clerks and strangers now often call any young woman "美女" simply to get her attention, similar to how English "miss" is used regardless of looks.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 距 relates to the distance covered on foot.
巨 (jù) is an exact match for the sound of 距.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

example.hanzi: 这两个城市之间的距离大约是三百公里。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè chéngshì zhījiān de jùlí dàyuē shì sānbǎi gōnglǐ.
example.english: The distance between these two cities is about three hundred kilometers.
example.fact: 距离 doubles as both a noun ("distance") and a verb ("to be apart from," as in 距离现在 "counting from now") — a common Mandarin pattern where a compound describing a spatial or temporal relationship can function like a preposition without needing a separate word.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 校长在开学典礼上讲话。
example.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zài kāixué diǎnlǐ shàng jiǎnghuà.
example.english: The principal gave a speech at the opening ceremony.
example.fact: 讲话 leans formal and public — a speech given at a ceremony or meeting — while its near-synonym 说话 is the neutral, everyday verb for ordinary talking; mixing the two up is a common register slip when narrating a meeting versus a casual chat.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

example.hanzi: 经过练习,他的水平有所提高。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò liànxí, tā de shuǐpíng yǒusuǒ tígāo.
example.english: After practice, his level improved somewhat.
example.fact: 有所 is a bound, formal adverb that must be followed by a two-syllable verb (有所提高 "improved somewhat," 有所了解 "have some understanding") — it never attaches to a one-syllable verb or stands alone, marking it as bookish, written-register vocabulary rather than casual speech.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 这部动画是由一家日本公司制作的。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù dònghuà shì yóu yì jiā Rìběn gōngsī zhìzuò de.
example.english: This animated film was produced by a Japanese company.
example.fact: 制作 implies a deliberate, often skilled or artistic process — used for films, handicrafts, or designed goods — distinguishing it from the more mechanical, bulk-scale 生产 ("to manufacture"), a distinction that matters when describing anything from a documentary to a factory product.

components.note: 行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 街上到处都是卖小吃的摊子。
example.pinyin: Jiēshang dàochù dōu shì mài xiǎochī de tānzi.
example.english: The street is full of snack stalls everywhere.
example.fact: 上 as a locative suffix (街上, 桌子上, 床上) turns a bare place-noun into "on/at [place]" — one of Mandarin's most productive grammar patterns for building location phrases, standing in for the prepositions English would use instead.

components.note: 才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 这个项目需要整个团队的努力。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù xūyào zhěnggè tuánduì de nǔlì.
example.english: This project needs the effort of the whole team.
example.fact: 团队 doubles up two words that both independently mean "a group" — 团 ("a group, a round mass," as in 团体) and 队 ("a line, a squad," as in 队伍) — reinforcing each other into one compound, the same word-building strategy behind 喜欢.

components.note: 日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'
尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù

example.hanzi: 我早就跟你说过这件事了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎojiù gēn nǐ shuōguò zhè jiàn shì le.
example.english: I told you about this a long time ago.
example.fact: 早就 stresses that something happened well before the relevant reference point, often with a hint of "I told you so" — its plainer cousin 已经 simply marks that an action is complete, without that extra emphasis on how far back in time it happened.

components.note: 自 (originally a picture of a nose) — 鼻 names the nose.
畀 (bì) gives a sound close to bí, differing only in tone.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 小孩子好奇地摸了摸自己的鼻子。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi hàoqí de mō le mō zìjǐ de bízi.
example.english: The child curiously touched his own nose.
example.fact: 鼻 alone already means "nose," built from 自 (originally itself a pictograph of a nose, later reassigned to mean "self") plus the phonetic 畀 — 子 is then added purely as the familiar noun-suffix seen in 孩子, turning a formal root into the everyday spoken word.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 他们俩相处得很融洽。
example.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ xiāngchǔ de hěn róngqià.
example.english: The two of them get along very well.
example.fact: 相 marks a mutual, reciprocal action shared between two or more parties (相处, 相爱 "to love each other," 相识 "to know each other") — it functions like a fixed reciprocal prefix similar to English "each other," and never appears with only one participant.

meanings: a modal particle indicating resignation or acceptance

components.note: 罒 (a net) — something trapped inside it.
去 (to leave, go) — unable to get away, together giving 罢 its meaning 'to stop, cease.'
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.

example.hanzi: 我只是开个玩笑罢了,别当真。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐshì kāi gè wánxiào bàle, bié dàngzhēn.
example.english: I was just making a joke, that's all — don't take it seriously.
example.fact: 罢了 sits at the very end of a sentence to downplay what was just said, much like English "that's all" tacked on afterward — it very often pairs with an earlier 只是 or 不过 ("只是...罢了") to double down on the minimizing tone.

components.note: 广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過

example.hanzi: 他们在海边度过了愉快的暑假。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài hǎibiān dùguò le yúkuài de shǔjià.
example.english: They spent a pleasant summer vacation at the beach.
example.fact: 度过 is reserved for living through a stretch of time (度过童年 "to spend one's childhood," 度过难关 "to get through a hard period") — it cannot be used for spending money, which instead takes 花 (花钱), a distinction that trips up learners who default to a single English verb "to spend."

components.note: 氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 注's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 很多网友都在关注这条新闻。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō wǎngyǒu dōu zài guānzhù zhè tiáo xīnwén.
example.english: Many netizens are following this news story.
example.fact: With the rise of social media, 关注 picked up the specific extra sense of "to follow" an account (关注他的微博 "follow his Weibo") — much the way English "follow" was repurposed for a new online action once Twitter and Instagram adopted it.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.

example.hanzi: 他去德国留学了三年。
example.pinyin: Tā qù Déguó liúxué le sān nián.
example.english: He studied abroad in Germany for three years.
example.fact: 德 here was chosen mainly for its sound, to transliterate "Deutsch" — but since 德 independently means "virtue, morality," it's a frequently noted coincidence that pairs it with other flattering-sounding transliterated country names, like 美国 ("beautiful country") and 英国 ("hero country," see also 英尺 in this batch).

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 大部分学生都同意这个建议。
example.pinyin: Dà bùfen xuésheng dōu tóngyì zhège jiànyì.
example.english: Most students agree with this suggestion.
example.fact: 大部分 sits at the high end of a scale of Mandarin "how much" words — 一部分 ("a portion"), 一半 ("half"), 大部分 ("most, the greater part"), 全部 ("all") — letting a speaker calibrate quantity without needing an exact percentage.

components.note: 穴 (hole/cave) — 窗 originally described an opening for light and air.
囱 (cōng) gives a sound distantly related to chuāng, having drifted apart over time.
户 (a simplified form of 戶) depicts a single door panel swinging on its hinge.

example.hanzi: 请把窗户打开,透透气。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chuānghu dǎkāi, tòu tou qì.
example.english: Please open the window to let some air in.
example.fact: 户 alone already means "a door, a household" (a pictograph of a single door panel), while 窗 alone already means "a window" — pairing near-synonyms this way, purely for two-syllable rhythm, is a common Mandarin compounding habit even when one half already covers the whole meaning.

meanings: variant of 奇蹟|奇迹[qi2 ji4]

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a rider.
可 here is said to depict a mount — a person riding in an unusual way gave 奇 its meaning 'strange, odd, remarkable.'
辶 (to walk) — 迹 names the trace left behind by walking.
亦 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to jī, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他能活下来真是个奇迹。
example.pinyin: Tā néng huó xiàlai zhēn shì gè qíjì.
example.english: It's truly a miracle that he survived.
example.fact: 迹 means "a trace, a footprint left behind" (built from 辶, "to walk") — 奇迹 literally reads as "a strange trace," the lingering evidence of something so unusual it seems to defy explanation, which is how the word settled into meaning "miracle."

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 山里的空气特别新鲜。
example.pinyin: Shān lǐ de kōngqì tèbié xīnxiān.
example.english: The air in the mountains is especially fresh.
example.fact: 空 ("empty, hollow space") plus 气 ("gas, breath, vapor") combine into "the gas that fills empty space" — a fittingly literal description of air, built from the same 气 root that appears in 天气 ("weather") and 运气 (rank 1162 in this batch, "luck").

components.note: 扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'

example.hanzi: 护士每天都要给病人量体温。
example.pinyin: Hùshi měitiān dōu yào gěi bìngrén liáng tǐwēn.
example.english: The nurse has to take patients' temperature every day.
example.fact: 士 as a suffix marks a trained professional or specialist (护士 "nurse," 战士 "soldier," 博士 "PhD holder") — the same root traces back to an old, respected class of literate specialists in ancient China, and also gives 士兵 "soldier" and 士气 "morale."

meanings: to share (esp. sth enjoyable, useful or beneficial)

components.note: 八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
亠 (a roof) — the top of a house.
口 (a mouth) — eating and enjoying inside it.
子 (a child) — together showing a family living and eating well under one roof, giving 享 its meaning 'to enjoy.'

example.hanzi: 她喜欢在网上分享自己的旅行照片。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài wǎng shàng fēnxiǎng zìjǐ de lǚxíng zhàopiàn.
example.english: She likes sharing her travel photos online.
example.fact: 分享 is reserved for sharing something enjoyable, useful, or emotionally positive (分享快乐 "share happiness," 分享经验 "share experience") — the dictionary gloss itself flags this with "esp. sth enjoyable," distinguishing it from plain 分 or 共享 for splitting up a cost or object more neutrally.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 被 originally meant a quilt or covering, like a blanket.
皮 (pí) gives a hint of the sound — 被 is pronounced bèi, a connection that has shifted over time.
扌 (hand) — 捕 describes catching something with the hands.
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound close to bǔ, sharing the same kind of initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 那名嫌疑人已经被捕。
example.pinyin: Nà míng xiányírén yǐjīng bèibǔ.
example.english: The suspect has already been arrested.
example.fact: 被 fronts the passive voice in Chinese (被捕, 被骗 "to be tricked," 被打 "to be hit") — historically 被 marked only misfortune or something done to someone against their will, which is why Chinese passive constructions still carry a faint negative flavor that English's neutral passive voice lacks.

components.note: Heart — regret is an emotional response.
Gives the sound měi, related to huǐ but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我很后悔当时没有多陪陪家人。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn hòuhuǐ dāngshí méiyǒu duō péi péi jiārén.
example.english: I really regret not spending more time with my family back then.
example.fact: 后 ("after, behind") plus 悔 ("remorse," built from 忄 "heart") combine literally into "regret felt afterward" — framing regret in Chinese explicitly as something realized only in hindsight, once it is too late to change the outcome.

components.note: 卬 depicts a person looking upward — 仰 keeps that upward gaze.
亻 (person) — a person 亻 looking upward 卬 gave 仰 its meaning 'to look up to, to admire.'

example.hanzi: 每个人都有权利选择自己的信仰。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu quánlì xuǎnzé zìjǐ de xìnyǎng.
example.english: Everyone has the right to choose their own beliefs.
example.fact: 信仰 is reserved for deep, often religious or ideological conviction (宗教信仰 "religious faith") — for an everyday "belief" or opinion about a fact, Chinese instead reaches for 相信 or 认为, keeping 信仰 for convictions that shape someone's whole worldview.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'

example.hanzi: 大楼门口站着两名保安。
example.pinyin: Dàlóu ménkǒu zhànzhe liǎng míng bǎo'ān.
example.english: Two security guards stand at the building's entrance.
example.fact: 保安 began as a verb phrase meaning "to protect and ensure safety" (保 "protect" + 安 "safety") — over time it also came to name the person whose job is exactly that, a purely descriptive phrase calcifying into a job title.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 态 relates to one's inner state, manner, or attitude
太 (tài) gives the sound — 态 is also pronounced tài, an exact match

example.hanzi: 蝴蝶是从毛毛虫变态而来的。
example.pinyin: Húdié shì cóng máomaochóng biàntài lái de.
example.english: Butterflies come from caterpillars through metamorphosis.
example.fact: 变态's original, neutral meaning is the biology term "metamorphosis" (变 "to change" + 态 "state, form") — its now-dominant colloquial sense, "perverted, abnormal," developed later as a figurative extension of "changed from the normal state," and the innocent biology usage still survives intact in scientific and textbook contexts.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 媒 originally described a woman who arranged marriages, 'a matchmaker.'
某 (mǒu) is only distantly related in sound to méi — the connection has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这件事引起了媒体的广泛关注。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǐnqǐ le méitǐ de guǎngfàn guānzhù.
example.english: This matter attracted widespread media attention.
example.fact: 媒 alone already means "a go-between, a matchmaker" (as in 媒人) — 媒体 extends that old sense of an intermediary connecting two parties to modern mass communication, recasting newspapers, TV, and the internet as the go-between that connects information to the public.

components.note: 走 (to walk, to run) — 赶 relates to pursuing or hurrying, both forms of movement.
干 (gān) gives a rhyme close to gǎn, with the tone shifted.
糸 (silk/thread) — 紧 relates to something pulled taut, as thread is pulled tight when spun, giving its meaning 'tight, tense'

example.hanzi: 快下雨了,我们赶紧回家吧。
example.pinyin: Kuài xiàyǔ le, wǒmen gǎnjǐn huí jiā ba.
example.english: It's about to rain, let's hurry home.
example.fact: 赶紧 always sits right before the verb it urges into action (赶紧走 "hurry and go," 赶紧吃 "hurry and eat") and cannot stand alone as a full predicate the way English "hurry!" can — its close cousin 赶快 is nearly interchangeable, differing mostly in a slightly more clipped, urgent register.

meanings: what is meant by the expression ...

components.note: 户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'
讠 (speech) — 谓 relates to saying or calling something.
胃 (wèi) gives the sound — an exact match with 谓.

example.hanzi: 这就是所谓的双赢局面。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiù shì suǒwèi de shuāngyíng júmiàn.
example.english: This is what's called a win-win situation.
example.fact: 所谓 can be entirely neutral, simply glossing a term before defining it ("所谓A,就是B" — "what is meant by A is B") — but placed directly before a noun in casual speech, it often tips into a skeptical or dismissive "so-called," the same slide English "so-called" makes from neutral definition to implied doubt.

components.note: 廴 (to move forward, extend) — 建 relates to constructing or setting something up over an extended process.
聿 (yù) gives a hint of the sound — 建 is pronounced jiàn, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.

example.hanzi: 两国正式建立了外交关系。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhèngshì jiànlì le wàijiāo guānxi.
example.english: The two countries formally established diplomatic relations.
example.fact: 建立 pairs a construction verb, 建 ("to build," as in 建筑), with 立 ("to stand up, to erect") to mean "to build and stand up" something abstract — relationships, systems, organizations — treating an institution as if it were a physical structure being erected.

components.note: 户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'
讠 (speech) — 谓 relates to saying or calling something.
胃 (wèi) gives the sound — an exact match with 谓.

example.hanzi: 你想去哪儿都无所谓,我都可以。
example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng qù nǎr dōu wú suǒwèi, wǒ dōu kěyǐ.
example.english: It doesn't matter to me where you want to go — I'm fine with anything.
example.fact: 无所谓 is literally 无 ("without") plus 所谓 (rank 1193 in this batch, "what is meant/called") — "there's nothing that could even be called [a problem]," a compositional path from "there's nothing to call it" to today's casual "whatever, I don't care."

example.hanzi: 这个城市这几年变化很大。
example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì zhè jǐ nián biànhuà hěn dà.
example.english: This city has changed a lot in the past few years.
example.fact: 变化 combines two overlapping "change" characters — 变 ("to change, to transform," also seen in 变态, rank 1190 of this batch) and 化 ("to transform, to turn into," as in 文化 "culture") — another instance of Mandarin's common two-near-synonym compounding pattern.

components.note: 毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 她不太会用语言表达自己的感情。
example.pinyin: Tā bú tài huì yòng yǔyán biǎodá zìjǐ de gǎnqíng.
example.english: She isn't very good at expressing her feelings in words.
example.fact: 表 ("outer surface," from a fur garment traditionally worn on the outside) plus 达 ("to reach, to arrive at") combine into "to bring something inner out to the surface and have it arrive [at another person]" — a vivid two-step image of communication as surfacing and delivering an inner feeling.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
纟 (thread) — 约 originally meant 'to bind, tie up,' extending to 'to agree, arrange' and 'approximately.'

example.hanzi: 从这里到机场大约要一个小时。
example.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào jīchǎng dàyuē yào yí gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: It takes about an hour to get from here to the airport.
example.fact: 约 alone already carries the sense of "approximately, to arrange an appointment" (as in 约会, "a date") — pairing it with 大 ("roughly, broadly") in 大约 reinforces the vagueness, making it Mandarin's default hedge word before a number, much like English "about" or "roughly."

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
车 (cart) — 辈 originally described a row of chariots traveling together, extending to a 'group, generation' of people.
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to bèi's reading, having drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他一辈子都住在这个小镇上。
example.pinyin: Tā yí bèizi dōu zhù zài zhège xiǎozhèn shàng.
example.english: He has lived in this small town his whole life.
example.fact: 辈子 literally means "a generation" (辈 originally described a row of chariots traveling together, later extended to "a generation of people") — 一辈子, "one generation['s worth of time]," became the standard way to say "a whole lifetime," distinct from the near-synonym 一生, which is built instead from 生 ("to be born, life").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 仅 relates to a person or amount limited to just this much, giving its meaning 'only, merely'
亻 (person) — 仅 relates to a person or amount limited to just this much, giving its meaning 'only, merely'

example.hanzi: 他仅仅用了三天就完成了这个项目。
example.pinyin: Tā jǐnjǐn yòng le sān tiān jiù wánchéng le zhège xiàngmù.
example.english: He completed this project in just three days.
example.fact: 仅仅 is just 仅 ("only, merely") reduplicated for emphasis, tightening the scope of "only" even further than 仅 alone — the same intensifying-through-reduplication strategy seen in 谢谢, which likewise doubles a single syllable.
